angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 598,302 km at 177.20 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6435 +/- 0.0189 mas (same row, RUWE 1.36): 177.20 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.86 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Santerne et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-29 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract): 598,302 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.94 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Santerne et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-29 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5358 +/- 38 K from Santerne et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-29 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Santerne et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-29 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-29.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.542, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
